events.text: Lanyon receives a registered letter from Henry Jekyll on the ninth of January.
events.quote: I received by the evening delivery a registered envelope, addressed in the hand of my colleague and old school companion, Henry Jekyll.

events.text: Jekyll begs Lanyon to help him, saying his life and reason are at stake.
events.quote: Lanyon, my life, my honour, my reason, are all at your mercy; if you fail me to-night, I am lost.

events.text: Jekyll orders Poole to wait with a locksmith for Lanyon's arrival.
events.quote: Poole, my butler, has his orders; you will find him waiting your arrival with a locksmith.

events.text: Jekyll instructs Lanyon to force open his cabinet and take the fourth drawer.
events.quote: The door of my cabinet is then to be forced; and you are to go in alone

events.text: Jekyll asks Lanyon to receive a midnight messenger and hand over the drawer.
events.quote: to admit with your own hand into the house a man who will present himself in my name

events.text: Jekyll warns that if the night passes without event, Lanyon has seen the last of him.
events.quote: if that night passes without event, you will know that you have seen the last of Henry Jekyll.

events.text: Lanyon suspects Jekyll is insane but feels bound to obey the appeal.
events.quote: I made sure my colleague was insane; but till that was proved beyond the possibility of doubt, I felt bound to do as he requested.

events.text: Lanyon drives to Jekyll's house, where the butler awaits him.
events.quote: I rose accordingly from table, got into a hansom, and drove straight to Jekyll’s house. The butler was awaiting my arrival

events.text: The carpenter and locksmith work two hours to open Jekyll's cabinet door.
events.quote: after two hour’s work, the door stood open

events.text: Lanyon takes the drawer, has it packed in straw and a sheet, and returns home.
events.quote: I took out the drawer, had it filled up with straw and tied in a sheet, and returned with it to Cavendish Square.

events.text: Lanyon examines the drawer's powders, phial, and book of dated experiments.
events.quote: Here I proceeded to examine its contents.

events.text: Lanyon dismisses his servants and loads an old revolver for self-defence.
events.quote: though I dismissed my servants to bed, I loaded an old revolver, that I might be found in some posture of self-defence

events.text: At midnight a small man knocks gently and crouches against the portico pillars.
events.quote: Twelve o’clock had scarce rung out over London, ere the knocker sounded very gently on the door.

events.text: Lanyon asks if the visitor comes from Dr. Jekyll, and the man gestures yes.
events.quote: “Are you come from Dr. Jekyll?” I asked.

events.text: The visitor glances back at a policeman and hurries inside.
events.quote: There was a policeman not far off, advancing with his bull’s eye open; and at the sight, I thought my visitor started and made greater haste.

events.text: Lanyon sees the visitor clearly for the first time and is struck by his appearance.
events.quote: Here, at last, I had a chance of clearly seeing him. I had never set eyes on him before, so much was certain.

events.text: 费莉西泰以每年一百法郎为欧班太太做厨娘和家务，并保持忠诚。
events.quote: Pour cent francs par an, elle faisait la cuisine et le ménage

events.text: 欧班太太嫁给一个没有财产的漂亮男子，他于1809年初去世，留下两个年幼孩子和大量债务。
events.quote: Elle avait épousé un beau garçon sans fortune, mort au commencement de 1809

events.text: 欧班太太卖掉房产，只留图克和热福斯两个农庄，年租最多五千法郎。
events.quote: elle vendit ses immeubles, sauf la ferme de Toucques et la ferme de Geffosses

events.text: 欧班太太离开圣梅莱纳的住宅，搬进市场后面一座较省钱的祖传房子。
events.quote: elle quitta sa maison de Saint-Melaine pour en habiter une autre moins dispendieuse

events.text: 费莉西泰黎明即起去望弥撒，一直工作到晚上。
events.quote: Elle se levait dès l'aube, pour ne pas manquer la messe, et travaillait jusqu'au soir sans interruption

events.text: 晚饭后收拾好碗碟关好门，她把柴火埋进灰里，手拿念珠在炉边入睡。
events.quote: elle enfouissait la bûche sous les cendres et s'endormait devant l'âtre, son rosaire à la main

events.text: 费莉西泰在讨价还价中最固执，锅子擦得锃亮令其他女仆绝望。
events.quote: Personne, dans les marchandages, ne montrait plus d'entêtement

events.text: 费莉西泰节俭，慢慢吃饭，用手指捡起桌上面包屑，吃专为她烤的十二斤面包。
events.quote: Econome, elle mangeait avec lenteur, et recueillait du doigt sur la table les miettes de son pain
